inflation_annual.source: Average of BLS CPI-U headline (3.7%) and core (2.6%, all items less food and energy), both 12 months ending Sep 2026, released 2026-10-14: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/cpi.htm. Chosen over headline alone because energy-driven spikes (energy +20.4%) usually fade over a 24-month horizon; not pure core because bills include utilities. Headline-only would be 3.7%.

raise_annual.source: BLS Employment Cost Index, private-industry wages and salaries, 12 months ending Sep 2026 (released 2026-10-30): https://www.bls.gov/news.release/eci.nr0.htm

ss_cola_annual.source: SSA 2027 cost-of-living adjustment, determined 2026-10-14, first payable Jan 2027: https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/latestCOLA.html (2026 was 2.8%). The engine applies it on the as_of anniversary, not in January.

rent_renewal_bump.source: BLS CPI rent of primary residence, U.S. city average, 12 months ending Sep 2026: https://www.bls.gov/charts/consumer-price-index/consumer-price-index-by-category.htm. National figure; regional releases were higher (Midwest 4.1%), so check before publishing.

forecast_paths.source: Design choice: Monte Carlo paths per forecast; a 24-month run takes well under 100ms at this size.

job_loss_monthly.source: BLS CPS labor force status flows, employed to unemployed, seasonally adjusted: monthly flow divided by beginning-of-month employment. Average of Jun-Jul, Jul-Aug, Aug-Sep and Sep-Oct 2026 (0.78%, 0.93%, 0.89%, 0.96%), computed from the counts at https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cps_flows_recent.htm (modified 2026-11-06). Includes people who quit into unemployment, so it slightly overstates involuntary job loss.

reemployment_monthly.source: Chosen so the expected spell matches BLS mean duration of unemployment, 27.1 weeks (about 6.2 months), Oct 2026, Table A-12: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.t12.htm (1 / 6.2 = 0.16). The raw CPS unemployed-to-employed flow is higher (about 25% a month, 23.6-26.4% over Jun-Oct 2026) but averages over a mix of short and long spells, which understates a long job loss; the median spell is 11.9 weeks. A memoryless chain cannot match both, and a stress test should not be optimistic.

ui_replacement.source: Pennsylvania L&I: 'Your Weekly Benefit Rate should equal about one-half of your full-time weekly wage': https://www.pa.gov/en/agencies/dli/resources/for-claimants-workers/benefits-information/benefit-guide . Applied to gross pay and treated as take-home (benefits are taxable; withholding is optional).

ui_weekly_cap.source: Highest rate in the Pennsylvania L&I 'Rate and Amount' chart ($604/week): https://www.pa.gov/en/agencies/dli/resources/for-claimants-workers/benefits-information/benefit-guide/eligibility-information . The chart is undated, so the 2026 maximum is UNCONFIRMED (some secondary sources say $605). Check before publishing.

ui_max_months.source: Pennsylvania regular UC pays up to 26 times the weekly rate (18-26 weeks depending on credit weeks), about 6 months: https://www.pa.gov/en/agencies/dli/resources/for-claimants-workers/benefits-information/benefit-guide . Assumes the full 26 weeks.

emergency_fund_months.source: Design choice: 3 months of essential expenses is the common minimum rule of thumb; the formula takes the target as an argument (6 is typical for one-earner or variable-income households).

starter_cushion.source: docs/rules.md section 6. Common personal-finance guideline for a starter emergency fund ($1,000), capped at one month of essentials when that is smaller. Not independently re-verified.

high_apr_threshold.source: docs/rules.md section 6. Design choice: above a typical long-run expected investment return, paying down debt is the better guaranteed return.

cushion_months.source: docs/rules.md section 6. Widely used planner guideline (3-6 months of essentials), lower end. Same figure as emergency_fund_months, which the job-loss stress test uses; kept as a separate key so the two can diverge.

cushion_months_high.source: docs/rules.md section 6. Upper end of the same 3-6 month guideline, for less stable situations: a paycheck-to-paycheck flag or dependents under the age limit.

retirement_target_pct.source: docs/rules.md section 6. Common retirement guideline of saving 15% of gross income including employer match (e.g. Fidelity's 15% guideline). Not independently re-verified.

card_low_cushion_apr.source: docs/rules.md section 6. Design choice: card interest at this level outweighs the risk of a thinner cushion, so a lump sum may go down to low_cushion_months, with a tradeoff flag.

low_cushion_months.source: docs/rules.md section 6. Floor for the card exception: one month of essentials.

mortgage_extra_rate.source: docs/rules.md section 6. Design choice: only mortgage rates above this compete with safe returns and investing, so extra mortgage payments are considered only above it (and only once waterfall steps 1-5 are done).

safe_savings_rate.source: docs/rules.md section 6. High-yield savings rate used across the app. DATASET-DERIVED, not a market quote: the median rate of the 22 high-yield savings accounts in the generated data (range 3.44%-4.14%), as of 2026-10-31. Check against current national high-yield savings averages before publishing.

snowball_small_balance.source: docs/rules.md section 6. Design choice for 'several small debts': a debt under this balance counts as small.

snowball_min_count.source: docs/rules.md section 6. Design choice: the snowball alternative is computed when at least this many debts are small.

idle_cash_months.source: docs/rules.md section 6. Design choice for 'more cash than needed': total liquid cash above this many months of essentials.

idle_checking_months.source: docs/rules.md section 6. Design choice for 'more cash than needed': checking balance above this many months of essentials.

cd_review_months.source: docs/rules.md section 6. Design choice: review a CD that matures within this many months.

credit_building_score.source: docs/rules.md section 6. Approximate subprime cutoff used by many lenders.

dependent_age_limit.source: docs/rules.md section 1 ('dependents under 18'): a dependent younger than this counts toward the 6-month cushion and the education step.

freed_payment_days.source: docs/rules.md section 3 (recently_freed_payment): a debt closed within, or a loan ending within, this many days. Look-ahead/look-back window chosen to match the 90-day forecast detail.

extra_paycheck_days.source: docs/rules.md section 3 (use_extra_paycheck): a three-paycheck month within this many days.

promo_expiry_days.source: docs/rules.md section 2 (promo_rate_expiring): flag a promotional-rate debt whose promotion ends within this many days. Same 90-day window as the other look-aheads. The dataset has no promotional debts yet.

automate_coverage_min.source: Design choice (docs/rules.md section 3, automate_savings): suggest automating savings when regular savings transfers cover less than this share of the monthly surplus.

retiree_investment_cover_months.source: Design choice (docs/rules.md section 1, step 4): a retiree whose retirement/investment accounts cover at least this many months of essentials has a drawdown backstop, so a thin cash cushion is not flagged. Withdrawals may be taxable; this is a planning simplification, not tax advice.

card_min_pct.source: Design choice for the payoff simulator: the common issuer minimum of 1% of the balance plus the month's interest (many issuers state it this way; some use 2% of balance, which would pay down faster). Not independently re-verified against a specific issuer.

card_min_floor.source: Design choice for the payoff simulator: the usual dollar floor on a card's minimum payment ($25-$35 across large issuers). Not independently re-verified against a specific issuer.

payoff_max_months.source: Design choice: payoff simulations stop after 30 years; a plan that has not cleared the debt by then is reported as not paying off (a minimum-only card can take longer).
